column5: Phase Milestones & Integration Gates
column6: Tracking epic.

column5: Publish Bid Processing service contract and interface spec
column6: Owner-published REST + event contract that all contributors code against. Freezes request/response shapes and error codes before implementation.

column5: Implement bid validation: eligibility, funds, auction-open checks
column6: Rejects bids from unverified accounts, closed auctions, insufficient funds, and below-increment amounts before any state change.

column5: Implement deterministic server-side conflict resolution for concurrent bids
column6: Authoritative server-side sequencing so simultaneous equal bids resolve identically on every replay. Removes dependence on client clocks and DB interleaving.

column5: Define bid rejection taxonomy and structured error responses
column6: Stable machine-readable rejection codes consumed by the frontend and the public REST API.

column5: Build concurrency test harness for contended single-auction bidding
column6: Reproducible harness driving 200 bids/sec at one auction, the contended case named in Section 3.

column5: Tune conflict resolution against week-9 load baseline
column6: Close the gap between measured p95 acknowledgement and the sub-500 ms target using the baseline curve.

column5: Implement auction lifecycle transition guards (bid, extend, close)
column6: Guards that reject illegal transitions and keep the orchestrator the single source of lifecycle truth.

column5: Build protection-window timer and auto-release scheduler
column6: Scheduled sweep that releases expired escrow holds within 5 minutes of window expiry and permanently closes the dispute option.

column5: Write contract tests: bid service to orchestrator
column6: Consumer-driven contract tests that fail CI when either side breaks the published contract.

column5: Author ADR: bid pipeline and deterministic conflict resolution
column6: Architecture decision record covering the sequencing choice, alternatives rejected, and consistency guarantees.

column5: Specify auction lifecycle state machine as a transition table
column6: Week-1 written specification of every state and transition before implementation begins, per the Section 10 risk mitigation.

column5: Design Kafka topics and implement bid-event producer
column6: Partitioned, ordered, replayable bid topic feeding both the bid pipeline and the fraud consumer.

column5: Implement Redis current-price buffer with batched persistence
column6: In-memory current-price reads and write buffering to remove single-hot-row write contention.

column5: Add idempotency-key handling to bid submission
column6: Guarantees a retried bid submission cannot double-apply.

column5: Implement anti-snipe auto-extension logic
column6: Extends the closing window when a bid lands inside the guard interval.

column5: Implement settlement transition: close to invoice to capture to escrow hold
column6: Orchestrated transition that generates the invoice, triggers capture, and moves the order into escrow hold.

column5: Implement invoice generation with flat convenience fee
column6: Invoice equals winning bid plus the single configured flat fee. Losing bidders are never charged.

column5: Implement escrow release and refund terminal transitions
column6: Terminal transitions after which the order is closed and no dispute may be opened.

column5: Build end-to-end auction lifecycle scenario suite
column6: KYC-gated listing through bid, settle, escrow hold, release. Runs in CI against the Compose stack.

column5: Document settlement state machine and publish ADR
column6: Final transition table with the time-accelerated fixture results attached.

column5: Build KYC document submission endpoints and validation
column6: Accepts seller identity documents with type, size, and MIME validation. Synthetic or consented samples only.

column5: Provision encrypted document store with time-limited signed URLs
column6: S3-compatible object storage encrypted at rest. Retrieval by signed URL only, never logged, purged at project end.

column5: Implement seller verification state machine
column6: Submitted, under review, verified, rejected, suspended, with auditable transitions.

column5: Enforce listing gate at the service layer
column6: Listing endpoint rejects any account not in the verified state, tested directly against the API rather than the UI.

column5: Implement bid-velocity tracking
column6: Rolling bid-rate measurement per auction feeding increment calculation and hot-auction flagging.

column5: Implement dynamic bid increment calculation
column6: Increment scales with velocity and current price to keep bid ladders sane under load.

column5: Implement hot-auction flagging and thresholds
column6: Flags contended auctions for prioritised buffering and monitoring.

column5: Unit-test and tune the pricing engine to 80 percent coverage
column6: Coverage plus behavioural tuning against replayed bid streams.

column5: Build PostgreSQL full-text search indexing
column6: Indexes listing title, description, and category with incremental refresh on listing change.

column5: Build search and filter query API
column6: Paginated query endpoint with category, price-range, and status filters.

column5: Write contract tests for KYC gate and pricing engine
column6: Verifies the listing gate holds and increments are deterministic across service boundaries.

column5: Author ADR: KYC data retention and lawful basis, plus pricing docs
column6: Records retention period, encryption, access path, and purge commitment for personal data.

column5: Define bid-event schema for the fraud stream
column6: Shared schema contract with the Kafka producer so one stream feeds both bidding and detection.

column5: Build labelled synthetic dataset generator: 500 auctions, 200 shill rings
column6: Built in weeks 1-3 before any detector exists, so the Section 9 recall and precision metric is measurable from the first iteration.

column5: Build streaming consumer scaffold on the bid topic
column6: Consumer group, offset management, and windowing primitives for in-flight scoring.

column5: Implement shill-bidding detector
column6: In-flight detection of seller-linked bidding patterns, raising alerts before auction close.

column5: Implement device fingerprinting signals
column6: Fingerprint features used as inputs to ring clustering and shill scoring.

column5: Implement bid-ring clustering
column6: Clusters colluding accounts across auctions from the live event stream.

column5: Implement fraud-triggered dispute creation and evidence linkage
column6: A flagged auction opens a dispute case with linked bid evidence and blocks settlement pending admin review.

column5: Build fraud metric evaluation harness
column6: Scores the detector against the seeded dataset and reports recall at fixed precision. Target recall 0.90 at precision 0.75.

column5: Write fraud detection design document and measured results
column6: Feature set, thresholds, and the measured curve, reported honestly if the target is missed.

column5: Define payment service interface with a mock adapter
column6: Payment sits behind an interface so Stripe is one adapter, not a demo dependency.

column5: Integrate Stripe test mode with manual capture
column6: Test-mode only, synthetic accounts, no real funds. Manual capture supplies the escrow primitive.

column5: Build flat convenience-fee engine with disclosure API
column6: Single configured flat amount per completed sale, exposed to the bid screen before a bid is placed.

column5: Build escrow ledger and hold transition
column6: Captured total is recorded as platform-held. No code path transfers funds to a seller outside the release transition.

column5: Implement Saga coordination and compensation paths
column6: Compensating actions for every money-moving step so a mid-transaction failure leaves no partial settlement.

column5: Handle Stripe webhooks with idempotency guards
column6: A retried webhook cannot double-release or double-refund.

column5: Implement escrow release execution for all three triggers
column6: Buyer confirmation, scheduled window expiry, and adjudication in the seller's favour, net of the retained fee.

column5: Implement refund execution and ledger reconciliation
column6: Reverses the capture through the provider on a buyer-favourable outcome and reconciles the ledger.

column5: Run 1000-settlement reconciliation test
column6: Every order must reconcile exactly and no order may be both released and refunded. Zero tolerance metric.

column5: Author settlement policy and escrow-simulation ADR
column6: States plainly that the platform never touches real money and the hold is an internal simulated record.

column5: Build bidding UI: auction detail and bid form
column6: Primary bidding surface with validation mirroring the service contract.

column5: Build live price display with flat fee disclosure
column6: Discloses the convenience fee that will be added if the bid wins, before the bid is placed.

column5: Integrate WebSocket client with reconnect and optimistic price updates
column6: Replaces polling with push, handling reconnect and out-of-order frames.

column5: Build KYC document upload flow
column6: Seller-facing upload with status feedback from the verification state machine.

column5: Build dispute submission form with evidence upload
column6: Available only while the protection window is open, mirroring the API rule.

column5: Build notification tray for outbid, KYC, and dispute events
column6: In-session alerts so an outbid buyer can counter-bid immediately.

column5: Build seller dashboard: listings, sales, payout status
column6: Shows escrow state and expected release date per order.

column5: Write frontend end-to-end tests
column6: Browser-level coverage of the bid, KYC, and dispute journeys.

column5: Write user manual and help guide with UI walkthrough
column6: Course deliverable. States that the escrow flow is a functional simulation.

column5: Build shared component library and design tokens
column6: Common primitives so all frontend contributors ship a consistent UI.

column5: Build login, registration, and profile screens
column6: Client surface for JWT issuance and refresh.

column5: Build admin KYC verification review queue
column6: Reviewer surface that approves or rejects submissions and drives the listing gate.

column5: Build listing review and moderation queue
column6: Admin review of new and reported listings.

column5: Build user suspension workflow
column6: Suspends accounts with reason codes and blocks re-listing.

column5: Build immutable audit log
column6: Append-only record of every administrative action, required for dispute adjudication evidence.

column5: Specify dispute lifecycle and build admin adjudication console
column6: Window enforcement, evidence review, and an outcome that either refunds the buyer or releases to the seller.

column5: Complete responsive layout and accessibility pass
column6: Mobile and tablet breakpoints plus keyboard and contrast checks.

column5: Write end-to-end tests for admin and adjudication flows
column6: Covers KYC approval, suspension, and both dispute outcomes.

column5: Write dispute policy and admin operations guide
column6: Documents the protection window, evidence rules, and adjudication outcomes.

column5: Write Dockerfiles per service and a single Docker Compose stack
column6: One image per service. A single Compose file reproduces the whole system locally and in CI.

column5: Provision Kafka as a Render private service with persistent disk
column6: Provisioned and smoke-tested in week 2 rather than at deployment time, since Render has no managed Kafka.

column5: Build GitHub Actions CI: lint, test, image build per PR
column6: Blocks merge on lint errors or coverage below 80 percent.

column5: Implement JWT issuance with access and refresh token rotation
column6: Stateless verification across services, carrying verification status as a claim.

column5: Build WebSocket gateway: connection management and auth handshake
column6: Authenticated connections with per-connection limits.

column5: Implement room fan-out and outbid alert dispatch
column6: Target is p95 under 100 ms from bid acceptance to watcher receipt with 500 concurrent watchers.

column5: Implement reconnect and backpressure handling
column6: Resumes state cleanly after a dropped connection without losing price updates.

column5: Build gateway middleware for role and verification-status gating
column6: Single enforcement point for roles and the KYC-verified claim.

column5: Configure object storage bucket with encryption and signed-URL policy
column6: Supports the KYC document store requirement.

column5: Configure Render Cron job runner for the escrow sweep
column6: Sweep runs as a cron job rather than an in-process timer so idle instances cannot skip it.

column5: Deploy all services via Render blueprint with managed Postgres and Key Value
column6: Each service deploys independently from its Dockerfile. Paid tier for demo weeks so services do not spin down.

column5: Deploy React SPA to Vercel with preview deployment per pull request
column6: Static build on a global CDN.

column5: Build Prometheus and Grafana dashboards
column6: Metrics and dashboards for bid throughput, latency, and escrow sweep health.

column5: Instrument distributed tracing with Jaeger
column6: Makes cross-service settlement paths observable enough to evaluate.

column5: Build load and soak test rig: 1000 bids per second, 500 watchers
column6: Run on a dedicated 8 vCPU / 16 GB host, not on Render or developer laptops.
